lineage: A UART receiver/transmitter with a bus-interface FSM: it synchronises to an asynchronous serial line (start-bit detection, mid-bit sampling, framing), a protocol state machine coping with timing and framing errors -- classic sequential control under timing pressure
version: github.com/freecores/uart2bus master as of 2026-09-12 (commit in hashes)
build_system: iverilog + a Techne testbench feeding serial frames
entry_points: the UART RX/TX FSM + the bus-command interpreter

example.command: Techne testbench: drive a serial byte at the configured baud, capture the received byte and framing-error flag
example.output: the decoded byte(s); framing error on a corrupted stop bit

human_capability_summary.built_to: receive asynchronous serial data with no shared clock -- detect the start bit, sample each bit at mid-period, check framing -- and turn decoded bytes into bus read/write commands
human_capability_summary.pressure: no shared clock between sender and receiver, clock drift, and line noise that corrupts bit timing and framing
human_capability_summary.success_means: correctly decoded bytes across clock drift, with framing errors flagged rather than silently mis-decoded

known_human_problem_solved: clock-domain-crossing serial reception and bus control
human_environmental_pressure: no shared clock, clock drift, line noise, tight bit-timing
human_failure_condition: mis-sampling a bit (drift/noise) silently corrupts the byte, or a missed start bit desynchronises the whole stream
behavioral_entry_point: skew the serial baud slightly from the receiver's, or corrupt a stop bit, and watch the framing-error flag / mis-decode

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run verilog-uart2bus
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: receive asynchronous serial data with no shared clock -- detect the start bit, sample each bit at mid-period, check framing -- and turn decoded bytes into bus read/write commands
